unanticipated_findings.summary: The RuleVersion union (PresentRuleVersion / MissingRuleVersion) is discriminated at 7 sites across 4 modules, including the byte-identical ternary 'method = "software_version" if isinstance(version, PresentRuleVersion) else "columns"' written twice, 26 lines apart.
unanticipated_findings.note: I grepped every PresentRuleVersion/MissingRuleVersion reference in src/. Exactly those 7 are discriminations (pipeline.py:121/146/147/150 are constructions, correctly excluded). The duplicated ternary at conversion.py:82 and :108 is verbatim. The report's claim that this is the stronger of its two findings on the bounds is well supported — 4 modules vs the trio's 1.

unanticipated_findings.summary: The default peptide-length pair is declared in three places and one copy disagrees: count_peptides defaults min_length=6 while everything else uses 7.
unanticipated_findings.note: Verified all three declarations. The 6 is real. The report's bound is honest too — it says the value is unreachable on the production path because resolve_protein_annotation_input always supplies one, and calls it 'not a live bug today'. Both runs found this independently.

unanticipated_findings.summary: adapters/anndata/fasta.py does a redundant double namespace read: has_search_parameters(target) and then require_search_parameters(target), to rebuild a union that read_search_parameters(target) already returns.
unanticipated_findings.note: The double call is exactly as described in the source. The claim that read_search_parameters already returns the equivalent union I did not open, so the 'redundant' half rests on the report's reading — but the two-reads-where-one-would-do observation is verifiable from the snippet alone.

unanticipated_findings.summary: The PeptideValidation union escapes past its factory and is re-discriminated verbatim twice in the adapter, manufacturing a str | None from a union that was split to avoid one.
unanticipated_findings.note: Verified byte-identical: both sites are 'result.reported_protein_field if isinstance(result, PeptideLevelValidationWithReportedProteins) else None'. Notably this run ranks it as a weak spillover ('two sites in one module, so weak on the bounds'), while old_skill ranks the same finding as the #1 thing to fix. Same fact, opposite priority.

unanticipated_findings.summary: MissingProteinSearchParameters is the third near-identical absent-search-parameters type in the package.
unanticipated_findings.note: All three classes exist at the cited lines. description.py in fact holds six Missing* identity types, so the pattern is broader than the report claims.

unanticipated_findings.summary: ParseRuleBuilder is not a Builder — it is a frozen dataclass with six required fields and one build() that filters candidates and raises on 0 or >1 matches; the name sends a reader hunting for machinery that is not there.
unanticipated_findings.note: Confirmed it is a frozen dataclass with required fields (no incremental construction, no stepwise interface). A naming/structure judgement rather than a defect, and the report says so ('cosmetic and not urgent').

unanticipated_findings.summary: Observability drift inside the trio: _resolve_cleavage logs a warning when it falls back to trypsin, while _resolve_minimum_length and _resolve_maximum_length substitute 7 and 30 silently; and resolve_cleavage_name has its own separate warn-then-fall-back-to-trypsin path, so the trypsin fallback is implemented twice with two different messages.
unanticipated_findings.note: The asymmetry in workflows/fasta.py is consistent with the source I read (the min/max paths end in a bare 'return _DEFAULT_*_LENGTH'). The second half — the duplicate trypsin fallback in resolve_cleavage_name — I did not open, so it is plausible but unverified by me.
